category_title: Middle school students who disengage and use ritualistic rule-following when encountering fractions
minimal_context: Idit is in a small group algebra course where the teacher has written an exercise on the board involving the addition of negative decimal and common fractions.

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: Let's look at the board. We need to solve this exercise: (-1.4) + (-1 3/4) + (-0.6).

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: (claps her hands, collapses her body) Oh! I can't stand fractions!

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: What do you think we should do first?

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: I'm bad at fractions and I can't stand fractions. Don't ask me, I'm not good with fractions. (smiles a bit toward her group mates)

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: Idit, can you try to do a part of it?

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: (Smiling) I think Ziv has to solve this exercise... (With decisiveness, turns back from facing the board to face her table) Me, without fractions!
